tools.metaDescription: Build a tailored recruiting outreach message that explains the role, why the person was chosen, and how to respond. Free private email tool by ReplyMind.
tools.h1: Write outreach that gets a real reply.
tools.intro: Recruiting outreach works when it sounds specific, respectful, and easy to answer. This tool helps you explain why the person matters for the role and what you want them to do next.

tools.subjectTemplate: A role that fits your background: {{roleTitle}}
tools.bodyTemplate:
Hi {{candidateName}},

I am reaching out about our {{roleTitle}} opening because {{whyThem}}. We are moving quickly and would value a short conversation if this sounds relevant.

{{nextStep}}. Our current timeline is {{timeline}}.

Best,
guidance: Name one concrete reason the person stands out instead of sending a generic sourced message.
Make the next step easy to understand by stating the ask in one sentence.
Keep the tone direct and human so the message feels like a real invitation, not a mass blast.
pitfalls: Do not stuff the message with every benefit of the company; the first reply is the goal.
Do not imply urgency unless the timeline is real and you can honor it.

examples.label: Passive design candidate
examples.input: candidateName: Mira; roleTitle: Senior Product Designer; whyThem: your portfolio shows strong systems thinking; nextStep: reply with a time for a 20-minute intro call; timeline: this week
examples.output:
Hi Mira,

I am reaching out about our Senior Product Designer opening because your portfolio shows strong systems thinking. We are moving quickly and would value a short conversation if this sounds relevant.

Reply with a time for a 20-minute intro call. Our current timeline is this week.

Best,

examples.output:
Hi Jordan,

I am reaching out about our Staff Backend Engineer opening because your platform work looks close to what we need. We are moving quickly and would value a short conversation if this sounds relevant.

Let me know if you want to compare notes. Our current timeline is next two weeks.

Best,

faqs.q: How specific should the outreach be?
faqs.a: Specific enough that the person can tell it is meant for them, but short enough that the ask is obvious within the first few lines.

faqs.q: Should I include salary in the first message?
faqs.a: Only if your process requires it or the range is already public. If not, focus first on the role fit and the conversation.

tools.intro: A good scheduling note removes friction. This tool helps you propose the screen, explain how long it takes, and tell the candidate exactly what to expect.

tools.subjectTemplate: Scheduling your first conversation for {{roleTitle}}
tools.bodyTemplate:
Hi {{candidateName}},

Thanks for your interest in the {{roleTitle}} role. I would like to set up a {{screenLength}} screen and can offer {{timeWindow}}.

{{prepNotes}}

Reply with the time that works best and I will send the calendar invite.

Best,
guidance: Put the available time window in plain language so the person can reply quickly.
Include any prep notes only if they are genuinely helpful for the conversation.
Keep the ask to one action: choose a time.
pitfalls: Do not bury the available times in a long paragraph.
Do not add vague instructions like 'be prepared' without saying what that means.

Reply with the time that works best and I will send the calendar invite.

faqs.q: Should I offer multiple time windows?
faqs.a: Yes, if you can honor them. A small set of real options usually gets a faster reply than an open-ended request.

faqs.q: Do I need prep notes?
faqs.a: Only when the candidate needs to bring something specific or when the call format is unusual.

{{prep}}

guidance: Restate the date and time clearly so there is no room for confusion.
List attendees when the candidate may want to prepare for the people involved.
Keep the message calm and factual; the invite already handles the logistics.
pitfalls: Do not assume the calendar invite is enough if there are special instructions.
Do not mix confirmation with evaluation feedback in the same note.

faqs.a: Yes, if the candidate needs to know where the interview happens or if there is any risk they may miss the link.

Use one gentle rescheduling path in case the candidate has a conflict.
pitfalls: Do not repeat the full hiring story or interview agenda.
Do not send a reminder so early that it loses its value.

faqs.a: Often yes. A short reminder reduces no-shows and lets people surface conflicts before the meeting starts.

faqs.q: Should I include prep questions?
faqs.a: Only if they are brief and truly helpful. The reminder should stay lighter than the confirmation.
